title: Positions on the bass and taking bass solos
summary: He says New Orleans players mostly stay in the first to third positions, and that he is not a bass soloist.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now when you play, well say all New Orleans bass players, take them for example, you know that they tend to play in first position, second position along and there or do they play it down below the seventh position or whatever it is on the bass?

Oh well that all depends on the bass player itself. I mean the majority of New Orleans bass players, I mean they tend to play in first to third position most of the time. But sometimes the number gets loose and you feel like showing off or you run around there because I mean I do it a lot of times myself. Well just like this Dixieland is supposed to be, you play it according to how you feel. If you feel like running down in case of them high notes, well I mean it's effective, it's very nice too.
What about solos on the bass? In the old days did they ever take many bass solos? They do occasionally now. Do you think it's a good idea?

Well, I couldn't boast it as a good idea. Then probably is a good idea because I like bass solos myself at times but I'm not a bass soloist. I mean I'm very clumsy when it comes to playing a bass solo because if they give me a solo, the only thing I will do with it is to keep up the beat and maintain the chord progression for the particular number that's being played. But as far as picking a melody or something through the number, I mean I've never, probably it's just my lack of practice of doing it that way but I never did, I never could make it fit in. And so for that reason I never did promote myself as a bass solos, I never was.
